title: Using Dataflow for Machine Learning Inference | EECS at UC Berkeley
content: Using Dataflow for Machine Learning Inference | EECS at UC Berkeley Using Dataflow for Machine Learning Inference Harikaran Subbaraj EECS Department, University of California, Berkeley Technical Report No. UCB/EECS-2020-75 May 28, 2020 http://www2.eecs.berkeley.edu/Pubs/TechRpts/2020/EECS-2020-75.pdf The need for systems to support machine learning inference has grown as the im- portance of machine learning in production systems has increased. Serving pipelines of machine learning models comes with challenges of scaling, low-latency require- ments for requests, and high computation costs for different stages of the pipeline. In this paper we propose that by taking a dataflow abstraction we can simplify and increase performance of serving these machine learning pipelines. The proposed system FLOWSERVEcombines this dataflow paradigm with Cloudburst, a stateful function as a service (FaaS) system to provide a framework to deploy and serve machine learning pipelines at scale. We provide several logical and physical opti- mizations that make FLOWSERVEoutperform currently used research and industry systems.
